questions.q: Which mosquito genus lays its eggs in floating rafts?
questions.e: Culex eggs are laid vertically side by side, forming a characteristic floating raft on the water surface.

questions.q: Sperm received during mating is stored by the female mosquito in organs called:
questions.e: Female mosquitoes store sperm in specialised organs called spermathecae for later fertilisation of eggs.

questions.q: The classical malaria symptom sequence of cold, hot, and sweating stages (paroxysms) corresponds to which biological event?
o: Synchronous rupture of infected red blood cells
questions.e: Paroxysms — the classic cold, hot, and sweating stage sequence — correspond to the synchronous rupture of infected red blood cells (schizogony) during the blood stage of the parasite's life cycle.

questions.q: What shape are the compound eyes of a mosquito?
questions.e: Mosquito compound eyes are kidney-shaped and made up of many light detectors called ommatidia.

questions.q: Which mode of reproduction, exemplified by the tsetse fly (Glossina spp.), involves eggs hatching within the female with larvae nourished internally and born directly?
questions.e: Viviparous reproduction in tsetse flies is critical for understanding African trypanosomiasis epidemiology, as larvae are nourished internally and born directly.

questions.q: Yersinia pestis, the causative agent of plague, is categorized in the lecture under which group of vector-borne pathogens?
questions.e: Yersinia pestis is a bacterium, listed alongside Borrelia and Rickettsia species as vector-borne bacteria.

questions.q: How long does it take for bed bug eggs to hatch?
questions.e: Bed bug eggs hatch after 8-11 days.

questions.q: Exopterygota undergo which type of metamorphosis?
questions.e: Exopterygota undergo gradual (incomplete) metamorphosis, termed hemimetabolism.

questions.q: How long do mosquitoes typically take to develop from egg to adult?
questions.e: Mosquitoes typically develop from egg to adult in about 7-14 days, depending on temperature and species.

questions.q: The arachnid body is divided into which two main regions?
questions.e: Arachnids have a two-part body: the prosoma (cephalothorax) and opisthosoma (abdomen).

questions.q: Millipedes belong to which arthropod class?
questions.e: Millipedes are classified under Diplopoda, distinct from centipedes (Chilopoda).

questions.q: What is the critical vector responsible for amplifying yellow fever into large urban epidemics?
questions.e: The urban cycle of yellow fever is driven by the highly domesticated, container-breeding Aedes aegypti, which bites a viremic human and can then transmit the virus widely among dense urban populations.

questions.q: The insect body is divided into how many main regions?
questions.e: Insects have a three-part body plan: head, thorax, and abdomen.

questions.q: A mosquito's longevity has little bearing on its ability to transmit malaria, since the parasite develops almost instantly inside the vector.
questions.e: Longevity matters greatly: the parasite requires time to complete its extrinsic incubation period inside the mosquito. A long adult lifespan is essential for the mosquito to survive long enough to become infectious and transmit the parasite.

questions.q: What is the correct sequence of mosquito development?
questions.e: The correct sequence is Egg, Larva, Pupa, Adult — mosquitoes undergo complete metamorphosis (holometabolism).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a symptom/effect associated with bed bug bites?
questions.e: Bed bug bites are associated with distress, anaemia, nervousness, insomnia, nausea, vomiting, chills, and iron deficiency in children - not joint deformity.

questions.q: Culex quinquefasciatus is a good vector for transmitting:
questions.e: Culex quinquefasciatus is the primary vector of Wuchereria bancrofti, the cause of most lymphatic filariasis cases.

questions.q: Mosquito larvae are primarily:
questions.e: Mosquito larvae are entirely aquatic, legless, and filter-feed on organic matter at or near the water surface.

questions.q: Approximately how long can adult bed bugs live?
questions.e: Adult bed bugs can live for relatively long periods, approximately 1-4 years.

questions.q: Target-site resistance of Anopheles to pyrethroids is caused by mutation of the:
questions.e: Pyrethroid target-site resistance arises from knockdown resistance (kdr) mutations in the voltage-gated sodium channel, the pyrethroid's target site. Cytochrome P450 and acetylcholinesterase changes relate to metabolic resistance instead.

questions.q: Which mosquito species forms the critical epidemiological bridge in the rural (intermediate) cycle of yellow fever, between viremic monkeys and humans?
questions.e: Aedes simpsoni, a semi-domestic species breeding in both tree holes and domestic containers, feeds on viremic monkeys that descend to forage near farms, then bites humans — bridging the forest reservoir and rural communities.

questions.q: In holometabolous insects such as mosquitoes, the larval stage typically occupies the same habitat as the adult.
questions.e: Holometabolous larvae and adults often occupy entirely different habitats — mosquito larvae are aquatic while adults are aerial — requiring separate control strategies.

questions.q: The exoskeleton of an insect is made up of:
questions.e: An insect's tough outer cuticle (exoskeleton) is composed of chitin, not collagen, cellulose, or keratin.

questions.q: Which region of the insect gut is the primary site of digestion and absorption, lined by the peritrophic membrane?
questions.e: The midgut is the primary digestion and absorption site, lined by the protective peritrophic membrane.

questions.q: Anopheles larvae, unlike culicine larvae, lack a:
questions.e: Anopheles larvae lack a respiratory siphon entirely; they breathe via paired spiracles and lie horizontally at the water surface, unlike culicine larvae which hang at an angle using a siphon.

questions.q: St. Louis Encephalitis and Japanese Encephalitis are both caused by viruses of which genus, and are primarily transmitted by which mosquito genus?
questions.e: Both St. Louis Encephalitis and Japanese Encephalitis are caused by Flaviviruses and are primarily transmitted by Culex mosquitoes, with wild birds (and pigs, for JE) serving as amplifying reservoir hosts.

questions.q: How many larval instars does an Anopheles larva pass through before pupation?
questions.e: Anopheles larvae pass through 4 instars, completing development in about 7 days in tropical conditions (up to 14 days in temperate regions).

questions.q: Which genus lays eggs in sticky, compact rosette-shaped masses attached to the undersides of aquatic plant leaves?
questions.e: Mansonia eggs are laid in sticky compact masses arranged in rosettes, attached to the undersides of aquatic plant leaves — a unique strategy linked to its plant-dependent larval stage.

questions.q: The Duffy antigen in humans affects susceptibility to which disease?
questions.e: Plasmodium vivax requires the Duffy antigen receptor to invade red blood cells; Duffy-negative individuals (common in Africa) are largely resistant to P. vivax malaria.

questions.q: Which mosquito genus is primarily responsible for filariasis transmission in urban, insanitary water in Ghana?
questions.e: Culex quinquefasciatus, breeding in polluted stagnant urban water (drains, ditches), is the primary vector of lymphatic filariasis in urban settings.

questions.q: How many sections (segments) make up the mosquito abdomen?
questions.e: The abdomen has 10 sections/segments.

questions.q: WHOPES-recommended insecticides for mosquito control include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.e: WHOPES recommends four classes: organochlorines, organophosphates, carbamates, and pyrethroids. Glyphosate is a herbicide, not an insecticide class.

questions.q: Which arthropod group is responsible for transmitting the greatest proportion of arboviruses globally?
questions.e: Mosquitoes transmit approximately 72% of arboviruses globally, making them by far the most important arthropod vector group for these viruses, followed distantly by ixodid ticks at around 18%.

questions.q: Haemolymph in insects can exert hydraulic pressure that assists processes like wing expansion after moulting.
questions.e: Haemolymph's mechanical role includes exerting hydraulic pressure that assists wing expansion, appendage extension, and eclosion from the pupal case.

questions.q: The key difference between crustaceans and insects is that crustaceans:
questions.e: Unlike insects, which excrete via Malpighian tubules, crustaceans excrete nitrogenous waste through the green gland (antennal gland).

questions.q: Infestation of the eyelashes by the pubic louse is termed:
questions.e: When the pubic louse infests the eyelashes, the condition is called pediculosis ciliaris.

questions.q: Body lice are described as 'gregarious', meaning they are typically found:
o: Clustered together, e.g. in clothing seams
questions.e: Body lice are gregarious, commonly found clustered together in the seams of clothing.

questions.q: Louse eggs are laid loosely and can easily fall off the hair or clothing.
questions.e: Louse eggs are firmly cemented/glued into place on hair shafts or clothing fibres, which is why they are hard to remove.

questions.q: Endophagic mosquitoes prefer to:
questions.e: Endophagic describes a mosquito that feeds indoors (en- = in, -phagic = feeding).

questions.q: The terminal fine tubes of the tracheal system that end directly in cells for gas exchange are called:
questions.e: Tracheoles are the finest terminal branches of the tracheal system, delivering oxygen directly to individual cells.

questions.q: Which secondary bacterial skin infection is mentioned as a complication of body louse infestation?
questions.e: Secondary bacterial infections such as impetigo may complicate body louse infestation.

questions.q: What shape is the bed bug's abdomen often compared to?
questions.e: The bed bug's abdomen is described as lemon shaped.

questions.q: Why are some Anopheles species more efficient malaria vectors than others?
o: Differences in feeding behaviour and host preference
Only female Anopheles exist in some populations
questions.e: Vector efficiency depends heavily on behavioural traits — anthropophilic feeding preference, endophagic/endophilic habits, and host contact patterns — which vary between Anopheles species.

questions.q: What disease is transmitted by the Mansonia mosquito?
questions.e: Mansonia africana and M. uniformis are key vectors of Wuchereria bancrofti, the cause of lymphatic filariasis.

questions.q: The halteres are a true second pair of flight wings used to generate lift.
questions.e: Halteres are modified hind wings used for balance and steering, not for generating lift; only the front pair of wings is used for flying.

questions.q: Compared with the body and head louse, the pubic louse is:
questions.e: The pubic louse is smaller than the other two types of lice.

questions.q: Larval source reduction, as a mosquito control method, refers to:
o: Eliminating stagnant water and breeding sites
Spraying insecticide on adult resting sites
questions.e: Source reduction means eliminating or modifying breeding sites (e.g. removing stagnant water), distinct from chemical control (spraying) or genetic control (sterile males).

questions.q: Roughly how many nits per day does a female head louse cement to hair, according to the epidemiology section?
questions.e: In the epidemiology section, the female head louse is described as living 1 month and laying 7-10 nits per day.

questions.q: What is the primary mode of transmission for the pubic louse?
questions.e: Pubic louse infestation occurs primarily through sexual contact.

questions.q: What type of atmosphere does the pubic louse prefer?
questions.e: The pubic louse prefers a humid atmosphere.

questions.q: What is required for each bed bug nymphal instar to progress to the next stage?
questions.e: Each nymphal instar requires at least one blood meal before it can moult to the next stage.

questions.q: The Malpighian tubule in insects is analogous to which organ in humans?
questions.e: Malpighian tubules regulate the osmotic and nitrogenous waste balance of the haemolymph, functionally analogous to the human kidney.

questions.q: Mosquitoes belong to which insect order?
questions.e: Mosquitoes belong to Order Diptera ('true flies'), Family Culicidae.

questions.q: What structure in mosquitoes is critical for detecting CO2 from a host?
questions.e: The maxillary palps carry the primary CO2-sensing receptors that help mosquitoes locate a host.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a function of insect haemolymph?
o: Carrying excretory products to excretory organs
questions.e: Insects lack haemoglobin; oxygen delivery occurs via the tracheal system through diffusion, not via haemolymph.

questions.q: The pupal stage of the Anopheles mosquito is non-feeding but remains highly mobile in water.
questions.e: True — the pupa does not feed, but it is highly mobile and retreats quickly from disturbance using its paddles.

questions.q: What characteristic odour is associated with a heavy bed bug infestation?
questions.e: A heavy bed bug infestation may produce a sickly sweet smell, likened to rotting raspberries.

questions.q: Hatching of the insect egg, marking the start of larval/nymphal life, is termed:
questions.e: Eclosion marks hatching from the egg, the beginning of the immature developmental stages.

questions.q: Which mosquito species is the primary vector of Wuchereria bancrofti in urban settings?
questions.e: Culex quinquefasciatus, which breeds prolifically in insanitary, stagnant, polluted water such as drains and open sewers, is the primary urban vector of Wuchereria bancrofti, the cause of most lymphatic filariasis.

questions.q: Which of the following arthropods has muscle-powered wings for locomotion?
questions.e: Among these options, only the mosquito (an insect) possesses wings; spiders, scorpions, and crabs do not fly.

questions.q: What is the most diagnostic visual feature of the genus Aedes, especially Ae. aegypti?
o: Plain brown coloration with no markings
Black-and-white silvery scale banding, including a lyre-shaped thoracic pattern
A single red stripe down the abdomen
questions.e: Aedes adults display a striking black-and-white silvery scale pattern, including banded ('ringed') legs and, in Ae. aegypti, a distinctive lyre-shaped white marking on the dorsal thorax.

questions.q: In the five-stage IVM process, what is the purpose of Stage 1 (Situation Analysis & Survey)?
o: To establish a baseline assessment defining the problem and evidence base
To distribute insecticide-treated nets to households
To train community health workers exclusively
questions.e: Stage 1, Situation Analysis & Survey, establishes a rigorous baseline assessment — identifying vector species, local ecology, resistance status, and socioeconomic context — that provides the evidence base for all subsequent program decisions.

questions.q: Which sexual distinction is true of male culicine mosquitoes compared to females?
o: Males have short palps and pilose antennae
Males have long palps and plumose antennae
questions.e: Male culicines have long palps and plumose (bushy) antennae used to detect female pheromones, whereas females have short palps, pilose antennae, and abdominal scales (a feature absent in Anopheles of either sex).

questions.q: Approximately how many eggs does a female head louse lay per day?
questions.e: The female head louse lays about 6-8 eggs per day.

questions.q: A female Anopheles mosquito bites man because:
o: She needs a blood meal for egg development
She is attracted to movement only
questions.e: Female mosquitoes need the protein from a blood meal to mature their eggs; this is why only females bite.

questions.q: Bed bugs belong to which insect Order?
questions.e: Bed bugs belong to the Order Hemiptera (the 'true bugs').

questions.q: Complete metamorphosis (holometabolism) is advantageous mainly because:
o: Larvae and adults occupy different niches, avoiding resource competition
Males are eliminated from the population
questions.e: Because larvae and adults look and behave completely differently (e.g. aquatic larvae vs. aerial adult mosquitoes), they exploit different habitats and resources, avoiding competition with each other.

questions.q: How many ventral maxillae stylets does the louse possess?
questions.e: The louse has 2 ventral maxillae stylets, which work alongside the mandible and hypopharynx.

questions.q: Where do the rudimentary, non-functional wings of the bed bug lie?
o: They are entirely absent, with no trace
questions.e: The rudimentary, non-functional wings (hemielytra) of the bed bug lie over the meso- and metathorax.

questions.q: Why are standard surface-applied larvicides generally ineffective against Mansonia larvae?
o: Mansonia larvae are resistant to all chemical compounds
Mansonia larvae obtain oxygen from plant tissue rather than the water surface
Mansonia larvae live exclusively on dry land
Mansonia larvae are too large to be affected by larvicides
questions.e: Because Mansonia larvae pierce aquatic plant tissue (such as water lettuce) for oxygen rather than surfacing, oil-based surface larvicides cannot reach them — control instead requires removing or treating the aquatic vegetation itself.

questions.q: An Anopheles mosquito's resting posture is characteristically at:
questions.e: Adult Anopheles rest at a sharp upward angle (45° or greater) to the surface — a key diagnostic field feature, distinguishing them from culicines, which rest parallel to the surface.

questions.q: Which population group is most commonly affected by head lice?
questions.e: Children are most commonly affected by head lice infestation.

questions.q: What sensory structure is used by mosquitoes to sense changes in wind current?
questions.e: Mosquito antennae detect CO2, body heat, and air currents.

questions.q: Culex pipiens fatigans, known as the 'rain barrel' or house mosquito, is the primary vector for which disease?
questions.e: Culex pipiens fatigans, the 'rain barrel' or house mosquito, is the primary vector of lymphatic filariasis and breeds strongly in insanitary, polluted water such as drains and ditches.

questions.q: The primary goal of the insect excretory system, achieved mainly via the Malpighian tubules, is to:
o: Maintain a constant internal environment by regulating pH and osmotic concentration
questions.e: The excretory system maintains homeostasis by regulating the pH and osmotic concentration of the haemolymph.

questions.q: How are louse nits typically described in shape and colour?
questions.e: Louse nits are oval and white, and possess a small lid called an operculum.

questions.q: In Endopterygota, wings develop:
questions.e: Endopterygote insects develop wings internally during the larval stage, emerging fully formed in the adult.

questions.q: What is the primary reason only female mosquitoes bite humans?
questions.e: True — only female mosquitoes require a blood meal (for egg protein); males feed on nectar and plant sugars.

questions.q: Which needle-like mouthpart structures penetrate the skin to reach blood vessels?
questions.e: The maxillae are needle-like structures that penetrate the skin to reach blood vessels.

questions.q: Which parasite listed in the lecture is the causative agent of African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness)?
questions.e: Trypanosoma brucei causes African trypanosomiasis, while T. cruzi causes Chagas disease in the Americas.

questions.q: How many larval instars (developmental stages) does a mosquito larva pass through?
questions.e: Mosquito larvae pass through four larval instars.

questions.q: How many segments make up the body louse's antennae?
questions.e: The body louse has short, 5-segmented antennae.

questions.q: Organophosphate insecticides generally have a longer residual activity (6–12 months) than pyrethroids.
questions.e: Organophosphates actually have a shorter residual activity of only 2–3 months, are biodegradable, and have low mammalian toxicity — unlike DDT-type organochlorines, which can persist for 6–12 months.

questions.q: Aedes aegypti is a primary vector of which disease(s)?
questions.e: Aedes aegypti is the primary vector of dengue, yellow fever, Zika, and chikungunya.

questions.q: In most non-blood-feeding insects, saliva primarily moistens the mouthparts and contains digestive enzymes such as amylase.
questions.e: Saliva normally moistens mouthparts and aids digestion (e.g., amylase in cockroaches); medically significant components like anticoagulins are most prominent in blood-feeding insects.

questions.q: Which of these is given as an example of a 'natural' mosquito breeding habitat?
questions.e: Natural habitats mentioned include tree holes and bamboo stumps.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a factor that attracts body lice to a host?
questions.e: Body lice are attracted by odour, sweat chemistry, body temperature, humidity, and darkness (e.g. beneath clothing) - not bright light.

questions.q: Halteres in mosquitoes function as:
questions.e: Halteres are modified hindwings that act as a gyroscopic organ, enabling balance and precise in-flight manoeuvring.

questions.q: Organophosphate insecticides are characterised by which of the following?
o: Very effective but with short residual activity of 2-3 months
High mammalian toxicity used only outdoors
questions.e: Organophosphates are very effective insecticides but have a short residual activity of about 2-3 months and are relatively expensive to produce.

questions.q: The shed exoskeleton left behind after moulting is referred to as the:
questions.e: The cast-off skin from moulting is called the exuviae.

questions.q: The insect alimentary canal is divided into how many main regions?
questions.e: The alimentary canal comprises three regions: foregut, midgut, and hindgut.

questions.q: Controlling mosquito populations by releasing sterile males to disrupt mating is known as:
questions.e: Sterile Insect Technique (SIT) suppresses populations by releasing sterile males that mate with wild females without producing viable offspring.

questions.q: The gonotrophic cycle refers to:
o: Blood feeding, egg maturation, and oviposition
questions.e: The gonotrophic cycle is the repeated cycle of blood feeding, egg maturation, and oviposition in female mosquitoes.

questions.q: Which insect sensory receptors are primarily responsible for taste and smell?
questions.e: Chemoreceptors, located on antennae and palps, are responsible for taste and smell.

questions.q: Why do Anopheles larvae lie parallel to the water surface?
o: To breathe via spiracles, since they lack a respiratory siphon
questions.e: Anopheles larvae lack a siphon entirely, so they lie horizontally at the surface to access air through paired spiracles on abdominal segment 8.

questions.q: Where does itching occur in pubic louse infestation?
o: Only in infested areas of the body
questions.e: Itching from pubic lice occurs only in the areas of the body that are infested.

questions.q: How long does the general louse egg stage last before hatching?
questions.e: The general louse egg stage lasts 6-10 days before hatching.

questions.q: Harmonic convergence in mosquito mating refers to:
o: Synchronisation of male and female wingbeat frequency
questions.e: Harmonic convergence is courtship behaviour where a male mosquito modulates his wingbeat frequency to match the female's.

questions.q: Bed bugs are described as 'gregarious', meaning they tend to:
questions.e: Bed bugs are gregarious in nature, often found aggregated together in harbourages.

questions.q: Which structures in the hindgut reabsorb up to 90% of water from the forming faecal pellet?
questions.e: Rectal papillae in the rectum reabsorb up to 90% of water, a key adaptation for water conservation.

questions.q: The most reliable way to distinguish between adult Anopheles and Culicine mosquitoes is to examine:
questions.e: Classic answer — Anopheles females have palps as long as the proboscis; Culicines have short palps.

questions.q: In Malaria:
o: the mosquito is the intermediate host
a common symptom in children is haematuria
cyclical development of the parasite in the mosquito is known as schizogony
sporozoites are chemically attracted to the red blood cells
Plasmodium falciparum causes benign tertian malaria
questions.e: Documented — associated with severe/blackwater fever presentations in children.

questions.q: Pediculus humanus capitis is associated with the following diseases:
questions.e: The infestation itself is termed pediculosis.

questions.q: Soft ticks:
o: have a capitulum that is visible dorsally
questions.e: Correct — most soft ticks lack eyes.

questions.q: When classifying Myiasis
o: Traumatic myiasis implies that the lesions are boil like
Facultative myiasis describes maggots that depend entirely on their host for survival
Enteric myiasis involves nasopharyngeal organs and tissues
Sanguinivorous myiasis denotes superficial attachment by maggots that feed on blood
Pseudomyiasis describes maggots burrowing in the skin such that their progress may be followed
questions.e: Correct — describes blood-feeding myiasis (e.g. Congo floor maggot pattern).

questions.q: Stomoxys calcitrans is a unique fly within the family Muscidae because
o: it's maggots are flattened dorsoventrally with fleshy protuberances all over
of the presence of a forwardly projecting proboscis
it has a hatchet cell on its wings
questions.e: Correct — unlike most Muscidae which sponge-feed, Stomoxys has a piercing proboscis for blood-feeding.

questions.q: In insects:
o: A gradual metamorphosis is known as holometabolous
The exoskeleton is rigid and prevents increase in size
A proboscis is only found in haematophagous insects
The function of the spermatheca is to produce a large number of spermatozoa
questions.e: This is exactly why insects must moult (ecdysis) periodically to grow.

questions.q: Besides the pubic area, to which of these sites can pubic lice spread?
o: Eyelashes, moustache, beard, chest, thighs, umbilicus
Only the soles of the feet
questions.e: Pubic lice may spread from the pubic area to the perineum, thighs, umbilicus, chest, moustache, beard, and eyelashes.

questions.q: In Onchocerciasis
o: there is enlargement of the spleen and liver
the diagnosis is by demonstrating the microfilaria in skin snips
questions.e: The classic diagnostic method.

questions.q: Sarcoptes scabiei mites
o: have four pairs of legs that end in suckers
are covered with peg like protuberances
questions.e: Correct — mites have cuticular spines/scales.

questions.q: In the Savannah areas of Africa, sleeping sickness
o: Is caused by Trypanosoma brucei gambiense
Is a Zoonosis with wild animals being the reservoir
Is transmitted through the bite of Glossina palpalis
Can be recognized by the presence of swollen cervical lymph nodes
questions.e: Correct — Rhodesian sleeping sickness is zoonotic, with wild game as reservoir.

questions.q: Cordylobia anthropophaga, the Tumbu fly
o: lays its eggs on soil contaminated by urine
questions.e: Correct — eggs are laid on soil/clothing contaminated with urine or sweat.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a common name for the body louse mentioned in the lecture?
questions.e: The body louse is called the clothing louse, gray back, or mechanized dandruff. 'Wall louse' is actually a nickname for the bed bug.

questions.q: The most reliable way to distinguish between adult Anopheles and Culicine mosquitoes is to examine:
questions.e: Classic answer — Anopheles females have palps as long as the proboscis; Culicines have short palps.

questions.q: The reproductively mature adult stage of an insect is also referred to as the:
questions.e: The adult insect stage is termed the imago, representing the reproductive stage with no further growth.

questions.q: To control a heavy infestation of Hard ticks on domestic animals it is best to:
questions.e: Habitat modification reduces tick harbourage — a valid method.

questions.q: Which leg is located farthest from the head?
questions.e: The hind leg is the leg farthest from the head.

questions.q: When classifying Myiasis
o: Enteric myiasis involves nasopharyngeal organs and tissues
Sanguinivorous myiasis denotes superficial attachment by maggots that feed on blood
Facultative myiasis describes maggots that depend entirely on their host for survival
Traumatic myiasis implies that the lesions are boil like
questions.e: Correct — describes blood-feeding myiasis (e.g. Congo floor maggot pattern).

questions.q: Sealing cracks, crevices, and gaps in a building to prevent bed bug harbourage is an example of:
questions.e: Sealing cracks and crevices to deny bed bugs hiding places is a form of structure proofing.

questions.q: All Anopheline Mosquito larvae possess
questions.e: Correct anatomical feature of anopheline larvae.

questions.q: Knowledge of the structure of the housefly proboscis is important to explain how the house fly feeds. The structural parts include
questions.e: Correct — part of the proboscis.

questions.q: The following stages of the Plasmodium parasite occurs in the Anopheles mosquito:
questions.e: Forms in the mosquito midgut after fertilisation.

questions.q: Cimex lectularius can best be controlled by
questions.e: A valid control method.

questions.q: Aedine eggs often remain in a state of Diapause. The following stimuli are required to break this diapause
questions.e: Temperature change can help trigger the end of diapause.

questions.q: In the life cycle of Simulium damnosum
o: The eggs are laid in communal oviposition sites
questions.e: Correct — established gregarious egg-laying behaviour.

questions.q: Untreated cases of louse-borne typhus may die as a result of:
o: Peripheral vascular collapse or bacterial pneumonia
questions.e: Untreated typhus cases may die from peripheral vascular collapse or bacterial pneumonia.

questions.q: Louse-borne relapsing fever is caused by which organism?
questions.e: Louse-borne relapsing fever is caused by the bacterium Borrelia recurrentis.

questions.q: Which of the following statements best describe cockroaches:
o: Both males and females possess anal stylets at the tip of the abdomen
The antennae of the cockroach is filiform
questions.e: Correct — long, thread-like antennae.

questions.q: Some of the distinguishing morphological characteristics of Hard ticks include
o: The presence of lateral eyes on the capitulum
The presence of a terminal capitulum
questions.e: Correct — hard ticks have a capitulum visible from above (dorsally terminal).

questions.q: The disease pathogens and parasites that houseflies can transmit due to their dirty habits include:
questions.e: Mechanically transmitted via contaminated fly parts.

questions.q: The life cycle of Tsetse flies is considered to be unique because:
o: The larval undergoes four larval instars in the female
all the development stages are internal
questions.e: Correct — tsetse are viviparous; the larva develops internally in the female.

questions.q: The most efficient control methods for tsetse flies include:
questions.e: A historically used control method.

questions.q: Which type of antennae is typically found in MALE mosquitoes?
questions.e: Male mosquitoes have plumose (densely feathery) antennae, which help them detect the wingbeat frequency of females.

questions.q: The distortion products created by combined male and female flight tones, important for mosquitoes to hear each other, are called:
questions.e: These distortion products are referred to as 'phantom tones'.

questions.q: The hard outer covering of a mosquito's body is called the:
questions.e: Insects, including mosquitoes, have a hard outer shell called an exoskeleton.

questions.q: Cockroaches are the mechanical vectors of pathogens like:
questions.e: Documented mechanical vector for this protozoan.

questions.q: The following terms best describe Phlebotomus sandflies adults general behaviour
questions.e: Sandflies are classically nocturnal/crepuscular biters.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the four mosquito life cycle stages?
questions.e: The mosquito life cycle proceeds Egg, then Larva, then Pupa, then Adult.

questions.q: The Onchocerciasis Control Programme was carried out for over 15 years because
o: The rivers in which the black fly breed were too long and inaccessible
There was a problem of insecticidal resistance
The parasite lives in the vector for a very long time
The West African countries involved could not raise enough funds
questions.e: Resistance to some larvicides emerged, prolonging the programme.

questions.q: Which of the following statements best describe the difference between insects and arachnids?
o: The presence of a waxy cuticle
questions.e: Arachnids have a fused cephalothorax; insects have separate head, thorax and abdomen.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT listed as an epidemiological factor associated with body louse infestation?
questions.e: Body louse epidemiology is linked to poverty, poor hygiene, and crowding - not high altitude.

questions.q: What shape and colour are mosquito eggs generally described as?
questions.e: Mosquito eggs are ovoid in shape and are black or brown in colour.

questions.q: Which insect order includes mosquitoes, blackflies, sandflies, and tsetse flies — vectors of malaria, filariasis, and sleeping sickness?
questions.e: Diptera (true flies) includes mosquitoes, blackflies, sandflies, and tsetse flies, all medically significant vectors.

questions.q: How many genera does the subfamily Culicinae contain?
questions.e: The subfamily Culicinae contains 38 genera (including Culex, Aedes, and Mansonia), making it far more diverse than the Anophelinae.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed among the major mosquito genera in the lecture?
questions.e: The genera listed were Anopheles, Aedes, Culex, Mansonia, Haemagogus and Sabethes. Stegomyia is an older subgenus name sometimes used for Aedes, not one of the genera listed.

questions.q: How is pubic louse transmission via fomites (inanimate objects) described, compared to sexual transmission?
questions.e: Transmission of the pubic louse via fomites is considered less likely compared to sexual transmission.

questions.q: In mosquitoes:
o: the most distinguishing feature is their rigid forwardly projecting proboscis
all anopheline larvae possess a siphon
questions.e: Correct — the classic mosquito identification feature.

questions.q: Which of the following is described as a typical mosquito breeding habitat?
o: Large permanent water bodies, small temporary pools, and natural sites like tree holes
questions.e: Habitats include large permanent water bodies (fresh, marshy, swampy), small temporary pools/puddles/drains, and natural sites such as tree holes and bamboo stumps.

questions.q: Which of the following statements best describe the life cycle of blackflies:
o: mature larvae remains sedentary for long periods of time
eggs are always laid in swift flowing water
prominent respiratory filaments are found on mature larvae
questions.e: Correct — Simulium breeds in fast-flowing streams/rapids.

questions.q: In insect classification the following are suborders of the order Diptera
questions.e: A genuine Diptera suborder — includes mosquitoes and blackflies.

questions.q: Fertilization in insects is internal, with mate-finding commonly mediated by pheromones.
questions.e: The lecture notes that sexes are almost always separate, fertilization is internal, and pheromones mediate mate finding across distances.

questions.q: In the sylvatic (jungle) cycle of yellow fever, which mosquito species maintains transmission among forest monkeys?
questions.e: Aedes africanus, a forest-dwelling, canopy-level mosquito, maintains continuous yellow fever transmission among monkey populations in the sylvatic (jungle) cycle, rarely descending to ground level.

questions.q: Which of the following flies are known to cause myiasis: cutaneous obligatory traumatic
questions.e: Classified among myiasis-associated flies in standard teaching.

questions.q: During the gonotrophic cycle in Mosquitoes:
o: two blood meals are needed for the eggs to mature
the eggs that are laid are able to withstand long periods of desiccation
the blood fed female seeks a suitable habitat to lay her eggs
questions.e: Correct — oviposition site-seeking is part of the cycle.

questions.q: Mechanical transmission of an arbovirus requires the virus to replicate inside the mosquito vector before it can be passed on.
questions.e: Mechanical transmission involves a virus being transferred on contaminated mouthparts without replicating in the vector. This contrasts with obligatory (biological) transmission, where the virus must replicate within the mosquito's tissues.

questions.q: What is the general complaint associated with head louse infestation?
questions.e: The general complaint with head louse infestation is the itch (pruritus).

questions.q: The following factors enhance the spread of Lice
questions.e: Classic risk factor — crowding facilitates transmission.

questions.q: Tsetse flies are easily recognized by
o: The presence of a rigid forwardly projecting proboscis
The presence of long maxillary palps
questions.e: Correct — classic tsetse identification feature.

questions.q: In the family Muscidae, the flies of greatest medical importance include
o: The greater housefly also known as Musca sorbens
Musca domestica also known as the latrine fly
Fannia canicularis, the lesser house fly
questions.e: Correct species and common name.

questions.q: Onchocerca volvulus, a parasite listed in the lecture, is the cause of:
questions.e: Onchocerca volvulus causes onchocerciasis, commonly known as river blindness.

questions.q: In Malaria:
o: cyclical development of the parasite in the mosquito is known as schizogony
sporozoites are chemically attracted to the red blood cells
a common symptom in children is haematuria
the mosquito is the intermediate host
questions.e: Documented — associated with severe/blackwater fever presentations in children.

questions.q: Mansonia larvae rise to the water surface to breathe atmospheric air, just like other culicine larvae.
questions.e: Mansonia larvae are an exception: they insert their sclerotized siphon directly into aquatic plant tissue to obtain oxygen and never surface to breathe, unlike typical culicine larvae.

questions.q: Which applied discipline integrates laboratory science with clinical care, identifying pathogens from patient specimens to guide therapy?
questions.e: Clinical Microbiology applies lab science to patient care, identifying pathogens and guiding therapeutic decisions.

questions.q: The most appropriate methods to control Houseflies include
questions.e: The primary housefly control method — removing breeding material (waste/faeces).

questions.q: Aedes mosquitoes involved in the transmission of yellow fever virus in Africa involve:
questions.e: Vector of the rural/intermediate yellow fever cycle (monkey-to-human bridge).

questions.q: Which class of Phylum Arthropoda is the largest and includes houseflies, mosquitoes, lice, and beetles?
questions.e: Class Insecta is the largest arthropod class and includes the medically important insects named.

questions.q: The network of internal air tubes through which insects breathe is called the:
questions.e: Insects breathe via the tracheal system, a network of internal air tubes delivering oxygen directly to tissues.

questions.q: Bites from Simulium damnosum
questions.e: Documented — blackfly bites are notably painful.

questions.q: Exopterygota undergo which type of metamorphosis?
questions.e: Exopterygota undergo gradual (incomplete) metamorphosis, termed hemimetabolism.

questions.q: Sucking lice, vectors of typhus and relapsing fever, belong to which insect order?
questions.e: Anoplura is the order of sucking lice, vectors of Rickettsia prowazekii (typhus) and relapsing fever.

questions.q: Dengue fever is colloquially known as 'breakbone fever' because of which clinical feature?
questions.e: Dengue's nickname 'breakbone fever' reflects the severe joint and bone pain that characterizes the classic illness, which is primarily transmitted by Aedes aegypti and increasingly Ae. albopictus.

questions.q: Arboviruses transmitted by mosquitoes can cause the following diseases
questions.e: A genuine mosquito-borne arbovirus disease.

questions.q: How many segments make up the larval abdomen?
questions.e: The larval abdomen is made up of 9 segments.

questions.q: Bed bugs:
o: when blood fed, turn a dark grey colour
questions.e: Correct — engorged bed bugs darken in colour.

questions.q: Which of the following statements best describe insects:
o: The malpighian tubules extract urine and other metabolic waste from the haemolymph
The main function of the haemolymph is to provide mechanical pressure
questions.e: Correct — Malpighian tubules are the main insect excretory organ.

questions.q: The pupal body is divided into the abdomen and which other fused region?
questions.e: The pupal body consists of a cephalothorax (fused head and thorax) and the abdomen.

questions.q: Pediculus humanus capitis is associated with the following diseases:
questions.e: The infestation itself is termed pediculosis.

questions.q: In Malaria Control Programmes the problems associated with conventional insecticidal spraying include
o: objection by residents in the home
questions.e: Documented issue — residents refusing indoor spraying.

questions.q: Which genus is most associated with malaria transmission in Ghana?
questions.e: Anopheles is the genus responsible for transmitting malaria, found throughout Ghana.

questions.q: Which member of the Anopheles gambiae complex is noted for feeding on both humans and animals and adapting to drier savanna environments?
questions.e: An. arabiensis feeds on both humans and animals (rather than being strictly anthropophilic) and is adapted to drier savanna environments, unlike the more anthropophilic, freshwater-breeding An. gambiae s.s.

questions.q: Yellow fever is caused by a virus belonging to which genus?
questions.e: Yellow fever is caused by a virus in the genus Flavivirus — the same genus that includes dengue, Zika, and West Nile viruses.

questions.q: Insecticides used in vector control are generally cheap and quick to develop.
questions.e: The lecture states that insecticides are expensive to produce and take a long time to produce and test.

questions.q: Louse-borne relapsing fever is also known by which alternative name?
questions.e: Louse-borne borreliosis is also known as Epidemic Relapsing Fever.

questions.q: Approximately how long does it take a mosquito to develop through its life cycle?
questions.e: Mosquitoes typically develop from egg to adult in about 7-14 days.

questions.q: The arachnid body is divided into which two main regions?
questions.e: Arachnids have a two-part body: the prosoma (cephalothorax) and opisthosoma (abdomen).

questions.q: Nitrogenous waste in most insects is excreted primarily in which water-conserving form?
questions.e: Most insects excrete nitrogenous waste as uric acid, a water-conserving adaptation for terrestrial life.

questions.q: Microfilarial periodicity refers to the rhythmic fluctuation in the number of microfilariae in peripheral blood over a 24-hour period.
questions.e: Periodicity describes the rhythmic 24-hour fluctuation in detectable microfilariae in peripheral blood, modulated by host circadian factors such as oxygen tension and body temperature.

questions.q: The pouch that houses the louse's piercing 'stabbing apparatus' is called the:
questions.e: The stylet sac contains the stabbing apparatus (the piercing stylets) used during feeding.

questions.q: The Anopheles gambiae sensu lato complex includes which of the following sibling species?
o: A. gambiae s.s., A. funestus, A. coluzzii, A. arabiensis
questions.e: The Anopheles gambiae s.l. complex includes sibling species A. gambiae s.s., A. funestus, A. coluzzii, and A. arabiensis.

questions.q: The body louse life cycle, involving gradual development without a pupal stage, is described as:
questions.e: Lice undergo incomplete metamorphosis, developing through nymphal instars rather than a pupal stage.

questions.q: Scabies infections can be confirmed by
o: preparing a thick or thin blood film and observing it under the microscope
observing skin scrapings under a microscope
questions.e: The gold-standard diagnostic method.

questions.q: All sibling species within the Anopheles gambiae complex are morphologically distinguishable using a standard light microscope.
questions.e: The species within the An. gambiae complex are morphologically near-identical (cryptic species). Differentiating them requires molecular identification techniques, despite their major differences in vector behavior and ecology.

questions.q: Which criterion is NOT listed as essential for a vector control method to be successfully adopted at the community level?
questions.e: Community-level methods must be effective, affordable, simple to apply, culturally acceptable, and safe. There is no requirement that the method be manufactured exclusively in high-income countries — in fact, locally available, low-cost solutions are preferred.

questions.q: Pediculus humanus corporis is considered to be a successful parasite because:
o: They have a soft pliable integument
The terminal abdominal segment is bilobed
The mouth parts lie close to the ventral integument
questions.e: Allows expansion of the abdomen after a blood meal.

questions.q: The following are examples of common Hard ticks found in Africa:
questions.e: A genuine hard tick found in Africa — a cattle tick.

questions.q: Which Anopheles species is described as highly anthropophilic, endophilic, long-lived, and a peak biter between 10 PM and 4 AM?
questions.e: Anopheles funestus is highly anthropophilic with a strong indoor feeding preference, is endophilic (rests indoors), long-lived, and bites nocturnally with a peak between 10 PM and 4 AM — making it a highly competent malaria vector.

questions.q: In Ghana, malaria transmission occurs only during the dry season and stops completely during the rains.
questions.e: In Ghana, malaria transmission is year-round but intensifies during the rainy seasons, when increased breeding sites become available for vector mosquitoes.

questions.q: Which bed bug species is known as the 'human bed bug' and has cosmopolitan distribution, found mainly in temperate zones?
questions.e: Cimex lectularius is the human bed bug, found mainly in temperate zones, with cosmopolitan distribution.

questions.q: In the gonotrophic cycle terminology, an abdomen that is large with both white and red colouring describes a mosquito that is:
questions.e: A 'half gravid' (semi-gravid) mosquito has an abdomen that is large, showing both white (developing eggs) and red (remaining blood) colouring.

questions.q: In the female mosquito, blood is temporarily stored in the:
questions.e: The crop is the structure shown storing a blood/sugar meal before it moves on for digestion.

questions.q: What is the general body shape of the adult bed bug?
questions.e: Adult bed bugs have an oval body shape.

questions.q: How many nymphal instars does the head louse undergo, similar to other lice?
questions.e: The head louse, like the other human lice, undergoes 3 nymphal instars.

questions.q: Culicoides grahamii can best be controlled by
questions.e: A valid control method — eliminating breeding sites.

questions.q: When are bed bugs most active in feeding on blood?
questions.e: Both sexes of bed bugs feed on blood especially at night, when they are most active.

questions.q: The characteristic forwardly projecting proboscis of a mosquito comprises of the following parts:
questions.e: Forms the sheath of the proboscis.

questions.q: Aedes aegypti is primarily a nocturnal, indoor-resting mosquito, similar to Anopheles funestus.
questions.e: Aedes aegypti is a vicious day-time biter, with peak activity at dawn and dusk, and is strongly exophilic and exophagic — feeding and resting outdoors — unlike the nocturnal, endophilic Anopheles funestus.

questions.q: Adult Anopheles mosquitoes typically rest with their bodies held parallel to the surface they are resting on.
questions.e: Adult Anopheles rest at a sharp upward angle (45° or greater) to the surface — a diagnostic field feature. It is culicines that rest with the body parallel to the surface.

questions.q: The human botfly, Dermatobia hominis is unique because:
o: Its pupa develop within the furuncle
It's larvae complete development within 30 weeks
The fly is dark-blue but has a yellow face
questions.e: Correct — the adult has reduced, non-functional mouthparts and does not feed.

questions.q: When do body lice typically feed on their human host?
questions.e: Body lice feeding occurs both day and night.

questions.q: Roughly how long does mosquito mating itself typically last?
questions.e: Mating itself is a brief affair, often lasting only a few seconds.

questions.q: The third segment of an insect leg is called the:
questions.e: The femur is the third segment of an insect leg.

questions.q: Some Anopheles species can also transmit lymphatic filariasis in addition to malaria.
questions.e: Beyond malaria, some Anopheles species transmit lymphatic filariasis (caused by Wuchereria bancrofti), which leads to chronic swelling and disfigurement affecting millions across the tropics.

questions.q: The following filarial worms cause Elephantiasis in man
questions.e: Causes lymphatic filariasis/elephantiasis.

questions.q: Inside the mosquito vector, filarial larvae develop through molts to reach which infective stage before transmission to a human host?
questions.e: Within the mosquito, filarial larvae develop through two molts over 10–14 days to reach the infective L3 stage, which migrates to the mouthparts and is deposited on the skin during the next blood meal.

questions.q: In honeybees, worker bees develop from unfertilized eggs while drones develop from fertilized eggs.
questions.e: It is the reverse: worker bees are produced from fertilized eggs, while drones (males) develop from unfertilized eggs (arrhenotoky).

questions.q: Which insecticide dust historically used for head louse treatment is mentioned in the lecture?
questions.e: DDT-based shampoos/dust are mentioned as part of historical head louse treatment.

questions.q: In Anopheles adults, how does the length of the maxillary palps compare to the proboscis?
o: Palps are much shorter than the proboscis in both sexes
Palps are equal in length to the proboscis in both males and females
Only males have long palps; females have short palps
Only females have long palps; males have short palps
questions.e: In Anopheles, both males and females possess long maxillary palps that are equal in length to the proboscis. This contrasts with culicines, where palp length differs distinctly between the sexes.

questions.q: In blood-sucking insects, which component of saliva prevents blood clotting at the bite site?
questions.e: Anticoagulins in saliva prevent clotting, maintaining blood flow during feeding in blood-sucking insects.

questions.q: Vector control methods suitable for community involvement should:
o: should involve vector control specialists and modern equipment
questions.e: A community method must actually work.

questions.q: Soft ticks:
o: have a capitulum that is visible dorsally
questions.e: Correct — most soft ticks lack eyes.

questions.q: Trench fever is typically fatal, with a high mortality rate.
questions.e: Trench fever is described as not fatal, although it can be incapacitating.

questions.q: Which pair(s) of legs in the pubic louse bear massive claws?
questions.e: The 2nd and 3rd pairs of legs have massive claws, while the 1st pair is small and slender.

questions.q: The key difference between crustaceans and insects is that crustaceans:
questions.e: Unlike insects, which excrete via Malpighian tubules, crustaceans excrete nitrogenous waste through the green gland (antennal gland).

questions.q: Even though the Onchocerciasis Control Programme has been heralded as a very successful project the major problems encountered include:
o: the ability of the Blackflies to fly long distances
inability to locate breeding sites of larvae
questions.e: Reinvasion via long-range blackfly dispersal was a genuine documented challenge.

questions.q: Adult body lice are described as very sensitive to body temperature.
questions.e: Adult body lice are very sensitive to body temperature, which influences their feeding and movement behaviour.

questions.q: Which thoracic segment is the largest in the bed bug?
o: All segments are equal in size
questions.e: The prothorax is larger than the mesothorax and metathorax in bed bugs.

questions.q: The different clinical forms of Leishmaniasis include:
questions.e: Visceral leishmaniasis — a genuine clinical form.

questions.q: Controlling mosquito populations by releasing sterile males to disrupt mating is known as:
questions.e: Sterile Insect Technique (SIT) suppresses populations by releasing sterile males that mate with wild females without producing viable offspring.

questions.q: A mosquito that rests indoors after feeding is described as:
questions.e: Endophilic describes a mosquito that rests/shelters indoors (-philic = preferring/loving).

questions.q: Which structure in the female insect reproductive system stores sperm, enabling fertilization over extended periods from a single mating?
questions.e: The spermatheca is a muscular pouch that receives and stores sperm, releasing it gradually to fertilize successive egg batches.

questions.q: Which structure forms a sheath enclosing the other mouthpart stylets and retracts during feeding?
questions.e: The labium forms a sheath (the visible proboscis casing) that encloses the other stylets and retracts as the stylets penetrate the skin.

questions.q: An infestation of scabies mites can best be treated by
questions.e: A traditional/classic scabies treatment.

questions.q: Approximately how many eggs does a female head louse lay over her lifetime?
questions.e: A female head louse lays about 300 eggs over her lifetime.

questions.q: Target-site resistance of Anopheles to pyrethroids is caused by mutation of the:
questions.e: Pyrethroid target-site resistance arises from knockdown resistance (kdr) mutations in the voltage-gated sodium channel, the pyrethroid's target site. Cytochrome P450 and acetylcholinesterase changes relate to metabolic resistance instead.

questions.q: Which sexual distinction is true of male culicine mosquitoes compared to females?
o: Males have short palps and pilose antennae
Males have long palps and plumose (bushy) antennae
questions.e: Male culicines have long palps and plumose (bushy) antennae used to detect female pheromones, whereas females have short palps, pilose antennae, and abdominal scales (a feature absent in Anopheles of either sex).

questions.q: Which control approach involves applying insecticide to interior walls and surfaces where mosquitoes rest after feeding?
questions.e: Indoor Residual Spraying (IRS) applies insecticide to interior walls and resting surfaces, killing mosquitoes after they feed and rest indoors. It is highly effective against endophilic species like many Anopheles, but less useful against exophilic species like Aedes.

questions.q: DEET (N,N-Diethyl-meta-toluamide) is best described as which type of vector control tool?
o: A larvicide applied to water bodies
A topical repellent that deters but does not kill mosquitoes
questions.e: DEET is the gold-standard repellent, providing the longest-lasting, broad-spectrum personal protection. Repellents create a chemical barrier that deters biting rather than killing the insect, and require frequent reapplication.

questions.q: External openings through which air enters the insect tracheal system are called:
questions.e: Spiracles are the external openings located on the meso- and metathoraces and abdominal segments.

questions.q: Saliva that helps the mosquito feed and can transmit pathogens is produced by the:
questions.e: The salivary glands produce the saliva injected into the host during feeding.

questions.q: Small body size in insects helps minimize food and shelter requirements, enabling survival in marginal environments.
questions.e: Small size is listed as one of the traits underlying insects' ecological dominance, alongside short life cycle, flight, and reproductive capacity.

questions.q: How many segments make up the abdomen of the body louse?
questions.e: The body louse abdomen has 9 segments with sclerotised (hardened) lateral margins.

questions.q: What is the chronic clinical hallmark of long-standing lymphatic filariasis, caused by blocked lymph flow?
questions.e: Adult filarial worms residing in lymphatic vessels block lymph flow, causing progressive lymphedema that, in severe long-standing cases, produces the grossly enlarged, hyperkeratotic limbs characteristic of elephantiasis.

questions.q: Which culicine genus lays eggs singly on damp substrate and is resistant to desiccation via diapause?
questions.e: Aedes eggs are laid singly on damp substrate at the waterline or in small containers and are highly resistant to desiccation through diapause, allowing them to remain viable for months without water.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of an Exopterygote (hemimetabolous) insect, per the lecture?
questions.e: Cockroaches, lice, and grasshoppers are given as examples of exopterygote insects with gradual metamorphosis.

questions.q: Chrysomya bezziana, the Old world screw worm is
questions.e: Correct — an obligate myiasis-causing species.

questions.q: Which transmission pattern describes malaria that is present at high, constant intensity throughout the year?
questions.e: Holoendemic transmission refers to year-round malaria transmission at very high, constant intensity, as opposed to hyperendemic (constantly high incidence), mesoendemic (seasonal), or hypoendemic (low incidence, epidemic-prone) patterns.

questions.q: Like the body louse, the bed bug's body is flattened in which orientation?
questions.e: Bed bugs are flattened dorsoventrally, similar to the body louse, allowing them to hide in narrow cracks.

questions.q: Culex decens is described as an important disease vector in Ghana.
questions.e: Culex decens is described as abundant but not implicated in disease transmission in Ghana.

questions.q: A mosquito that is mainly active at dawn/dusk is described as:
questions.e: Crepuscular describes activity that peaks at twilight - dawn and dusk.

questions.q: Which of these is listed as an additional bed bug control measure besides structure proofing and chemical control?
questions.e: Impregnated bed nets are listed as another control method against bed bugs.

questions.q: Draining or modifying breeding sites to prevent mosquito development is an example of:
questions.e: Habitat change/source reduction is classified as physical control.

questions.q: The scientific study of micro-organisms too small to be seen with the naked eye is called:
questions.e: Microbiology is the scientific study of micro-organisms — bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa, and algae — invisible to the naked eye.

questions.q: Which discipline is defined as the study of microorganisms that cause human disease, including pathogenesis and host immune response?
questions.e: Medical Microbiology focuses on disease-causing microorganisms, the nature of infection, host immune response, and treatment principles.

questions.q: Which applied discipline integrates laboratory science with clinical care, identifying pathogens from patient specimens to guide therapy?
questions.e: Clinical Microbiology applies lab science to patient care, identifying pathogens and guiding therapeutic decisions.

questions.q: The study of eukaryotic parasites such as protozoa and helminths and their impact on human health is called:
questions.e: Parasitology covers eukaryotic parasites, including protozoa and helminths.

questions.q: The Malpighian tubule in insects is analogous to which organ in humans?
questions.e: Entomology, in the medical context, studies insects and arthropods of medical significance, particularly disease vectors.

questions.q: Entomology is merely a zoological curiosity with little real relevance to clinical microbiology.
questions.e: The lecture stresses that entomology is a critical pillar of medical and clinical microbiology, since most devastating infectious diseases worldwide are vector-borne.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed among the vector-borne viruses discussed in the lecture?
questions.e: Hepatitis B is bloodborne/sexually transmitted, not among the arthropod-vectored viruses listed (which include Dengue, Zika, and West Nile).

questions.q: Yersinia pestis, the causative agent of plague, is categorized in the lecture under which group of vector-borne pathogens?
questions.e: Yersinia pestis is a bacterium, listed alongside Borrelia and Rickettsia species as vector-borne bacteria.

questions.q: Which parasite listed in the lecture is the causative agent of African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness)?
questions.e: Trypanosoma brucei causes African trypanosomiasis, while T. cruzi causes Chagas disease in the Americas.

questions.q: Wuchereria bancrofti and Brugia malayi/timori, listed among vector-borne parasites, are associated with which condition?
questions.e: Wuchereria bancrofti and Brugia species are filarial worms that cause lymphatic filariasis.

questions.q: Onchocerca volvulus, a parasite listed in the lecture, is the cause of:
questions.e: Onchocerca volvulus causes onchocerciasis, commonly known as river blindness.

questions.q: All arthropods share a common body plan featuring a protective exoskeleton called the cuticle and jointed appendages.
questions.e: Arthropods share a tough outer cuticle (exoskeleton) and jointed appendages such as legs and antennae as defining features.

questions.q: Approximately what percentage of all known animal species do arthropods comprise?
questions.e: Arthropods make up roughly 85% of all known animal species, with over 1 million described species.

questions.q: Which class of Phylum Arthropoda is the largest and includes houseflies, mosquitoes, lice, and beetles?
questions.e: Class Insecta is the largest arthropod class and includes the medically important insects named.

questions.q: Millipedes belong to which arthropod class?
questions.e: These organisms belong to Class Arachnida, an important group of disease vectors.

questions.q: Which arthropod group is responsible for transmitting the greatest proportion of arboviruses globally?
questions.e: Millipedes are classified under Diplopoda, distinct from centipedes (Chilopoda).

questions.q: How many pairs of legs do insects (Class Insecta) typically have?
questions.e: Insects have 3 pairs of legs (6 legs total), one of the defining features of the class.

questions.q: How many pairs of legs do arachnids (Class Arachnida) typically have?
questions.e: Arachnids have 4 pairs of legs (8 legs total), distinguishing them from insects.

questions.q: The insect body is divided into how many main regions?
questions.e: Insects have a three-part body plan: head, thorax, and abdomen.

questions.q: The arachnid body is divided into which two main regions?
questions.e: Arachnids have a two-part body: the prosoma (cephalothorax) and opisthosoma (abdomen).

questions.q: The key difference between crustaceans and insects is that crustaceans:
questions.e: Insects respire via a tracheal system that delivers air directly to tissues.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a trait contributing to insects' extraordinary evolutionary success?
questions.e: Small (not large) body size is listed as advantageous, minimizing food and shelter requirements for survival in marginal environments.

questions.q: Small body size in insects helps minimize food and shelter requirements, enabling survival in marginal environments.
questions.e: Small size is listed as one of the traits underlying insects' ecological dominance, alongside short life cycle, flight, and reproductive capacity.

questions.q: Mosquitoes belong to which insect order?
questions.e: Diptera (true flies) includes mosquitoes, blackflies, sandflies, and tsetse flies, all medically significant vectors.

questions.q: Sucking lice, vectors of typhus and relapsing fever, belong to which insect order?
questions.e: Anoplura is the order of sucking lice, vectors of Rickettsia prowazekii (typhus) and relapsing fever.

questions.q: Cockroaches, mechanical vectors of enteric pathogens, belong to which order?
questions.e: Cockroaches are classified under Dictyoptera and act as mechanical vectors of enteric pathogens.

questions.q: Bees and ants, significant sources of allergens with anaphylaxis risk, belong to which order?
questions.e: Hymenoptera includes bees and ants, notable for their allergenic potential.

questions.q: Winged insects that undergo metamorphosis are grouped under:
questions.e: Pterygota refers to winged insects, further subdivided by metamorphosis type into Exopterygota and Endopterygota.

questions.q: In Exopterygota, wings develop:
questions.e: Exopterygote insects show external wing development, visible even in immature nymphal stages.

questions.q: In Endopterygota, wings develop:
questions.e: Endopterygote insects develop wings internally during the larval stage, emerging fully formed in the adult.

questions.q: Exopterygota undergo which type of metamorphosis?
questions.e: Exopterygota undergo gradual (incomplete) metamorphosis, termed hemimetabolism.

questions.q: Complete metamorphosis (holometabolism) is advantageous mainly because:
o: Larvae and adults occupy different niches, avoiding resource competition
Males are eliminated from the population
questions.e: Endopterygota undergo complete metamorphosis, termed holometabolism.

questions.q: In the five-stage IVM process, what is the purpose of Stage 1 (Situation Analysis & Survey)?
o: To distribute insecticide-treated nets to households
To establish a baseline assessment defining the problem and evidence base

questions.q: The fluid that fills the insect haemocoel and performs the combined functions of blood and lymph is called:

questions.q: The only true blood vessel in insects, comprising a posterior heart and anterior aorta, is the:

questions.q: Valve-like openings in the insect heart that allow haemolymph to enter during diastole are called:
questions.e: Ostia are valve-like openings in the heart permitting haemolymph entry during diastole.

questions.q: The network of internal air tubes through which insects breathe is called the:
questions.e: Insects breathe via the tracheal system, a network of internal air tubes delivering oxygen directly to tissues.

questions.q: External openings through which air enters the insect tracheal system are called:
questions.e: Spiracles are the external openings located on the meso- and metathoraces and abdominal segments.

questions.q: The terminal fine tubes of the tracheal system that end directly in cells for gas exchange are called:
questions.e: Tracheoles are the finest terminal branches of the tracheal system, delivering oxygen directly to individual cells.

questions.q: Spiracle valves open and close primarily to regulate:
questions.e: Spiracle valves regulate water loss, a critical function in hot, dry environments where conserving moisture is essential.

questions.q: Which region of the insect gut is the primary site of digestion and absorption, lined by the peritrophic membrane?

questions.q: Which salivary component is responsible for the characteristic itch and wheal of insect bites?
questions.e: Allergens in saliva trigger local hypersensitivity reactions, producing the itch and wheal typical of insect bites.

questions.q: Nitrogenous waste in most insects is excreted primarily in which water-conserving form?
questions.e: Most insects excrete nitrogenous waste as uric acid, a water-conserving adaptation for terrestrial life.

questions.q: The primary goal of the insect excretory system, achieved mainly via the Malpighian tubules, is to:
o: Maintain a constant internal environment by regulating pH and osmotic concentration
questions.e: The excretory system maintains homeostasis by regulating the pH and osmotic concentration of the haemolymph.

questions.q: Which structure in the female insect reproductive system stores sperm, enabling fertilization over extended periods from a single mating?
questions.e: The spermatheca is a muscular pouch that receives and stores sperm, releasing it gradually to fertilize successive egg batches.

questions.q: Accessory glands in the female insect reproductive system primarily secrete materials used for:

questions.e: Female accessory glands secrete waterproof and adhesive materials that protect eggs and fix them to substrates.

questions.q: How many nymphal instars does the head louse undergo, similar to other lice?
